title: Pair-code validity in linear time
statement: There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean string $x$, $M$ halts within $c(|x|+1)$ steps and outputs the one-bit string whose bit is true exactly when the pair parser succeeds on $x$.
hypotheses_covered: a finite Turing machine and constant exist
correct one-bit output for every input
replaced:
There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and a constant $c$ such that $M$
computes, within $c\,(n+1)$ steps on inputs of length $n$, the one-bit
function recording whether the input is a valid word of the self-delimiting
pair code.
